verdict.line: You lose if you trade autos into Counter Strike or let Relentless Assault stacks run uncontested; you win by dumping Q-W-E through his stance and all-inning whenever E (Counter Strike) is down.

brief.thesis: Aatrox holds both the lane edge and the solo-kill edge here (52.8% over 229 games) because Jax's only defensive tool, E (Counter Strike, cooldown 18/16/14/12/10s), only dodges basic attacks and reduces area damage — it does nothing to your Q, W, or E, so committing full ability combos through it still lands clean. Jax has to physically close the gap with Q (Leap Strike, cooldown 17/14/11/8/5s, range 700) to do anything, and Aatrox's whole kit is built to make him regret that dash.

theirWindow.when: he leaps in with W (Empower) active
theirWindow.what: His empowered Leap Strike-auto or Empower-auto hits hard, and he can juke a raw auto-attack all-in with Counter Strike — hold your ability damage rather than walking up for autos so his dodge whiffs on nothing.

yourWindow.when: his E (Counter Strike) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: This is your all-in window — at rank 1 that's a full 18 seconds with no stun or dodge available. Land W (Infernal Chains) to drag him in, then dump Q swings and use E (Umbral Dash) to heal off the trade.

runes.keystoneWhy: Sustained melee trades and all-in stacking damage/healing fit dueling Jax, where you want to win extended exchanges before his R ramps.

summoners.why: The most-run and highest-winrate page for this matchup (51.9% WR, 70% pick) — Ignite converts your all-in windows into actual kills when Jax tries to walk away, and Flash lets you reposition Infernal Chains or dodge a Counter Strike stun.

playing.title: Bait Leap Strike before punishing
playing.detail: Jax's Q (Leap Strike, cooldown 17/14/11/8/5s, range 700) is his only gap closer — once he burns it to engage, immediately land W (Infernal Chains) since he has no way to disengage until Q is back up.

playing.title: Swing skills, not autos, into E
playing.detail: Jax's E (Counter Strike) only dodges basic attacks and reduces area damage — your Q, W, and E all still connect through it, so all-in with abilities rather than walking up for autos when you see the stance activate.

playing.title: Track his W before trading
playing.detail: W (Empower, cooldown 7/6/5/4/3s) buffs his next attack or Leap Strike — if he's clearly holding an auto or resetting distance, expect a harder poke or engage and delay your own trade until it's spent.

playing.title: All-in during his E cooldown
playing.detail: Counter Strike starts at an 18-second cooldown at rank 1 and only drops to 10s at max rank — every time he burns it defensively or to poke, that's your window to commit the full Q-W-E-R combo.

playing.title: Weave Deathbringer Stance into trades
playing.detail: Your passive empowered auto deals bonus magic damage and heals based on Jax's max health — landing it inside every trade both closes the damage gap and outsustains his healthless early kit.

playing.title: Grab anti-heal only if he pulls ahead
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this matchup calls for Bramble Vest or Executioner's Calling — pick one up if Jax starts winning trades off lifesteal, but don't delay your Eclipse spike for it while you're still ahead.

playing.title: Don't fight through his attack-speed stacks
playing.detail: R (Relentless Assault) passively grants attack speed on hits with bonus damage every third consecutive attack — disengage after your burst window instead of standing in extended autoattack exchanges where his ramp catches up.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and win-rate figures are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (229-game sample for this matchup); the mechanical reads on cooldowns, trade windows, and combat patterns are my own tactical analysis.

stats.opponentTip: Use [W] when Jax closes in using Leap Strike (Q). Try to deal bursts of damage by using your skills. Purchase Bramble Vest or Executioner’s Calling.
